correctness.rationale: The Palm stationary renewal occupation identity gives driving-force covariance D E[(T-h)_+²]/m for positive h; integrating the exact harmonic kernel yields Eq. (1). Strict ordinary Jensen for exp(-mu T) and size-biased Jensen for g(t)=(1-exp(-mu t))/t give the two strict endpoints. The two-point family has exactly the prescribed moments, reaches both endpoint limits, and by continuity realizes every interior variance. For s=m² only deterministic renewal is possible. The stationary solution exists in L² under finite E[T²]. The bundled standard-library reproducibility script passed 310 finite algebraic, quadrature and inequality checks; these checks are supporting evidence only.

value.rationale: The precise first and second reset-interval moments are natural experimentally controllable constraints on renewal timing. The result solves the complete attainable stationary variance problem at those constraints, shows sharp yet physically nonattained limits, and produces every intermediate target variance with only two positive waiting durations. Pointwise covariance convex-order monotonicity explains why renewal irregularity increases filtered fluctuations; the comparison distinguishes stationary phase averaging from prior reset-epoch observables.
